answer: Each identity installs a key-bound rain gauge capped with a velvet seal and locks an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it sends a beacon pulse with its peak-trough readings, serial, and a violet dye marker proving origin. An auditor recomputes the range from the rainfall table; a range off by over 5%, a reused serial, or a copied pulse burns the bond. The first gauge costs 34, the kth costs 34+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6028; 1000 fakes cost 3,031,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-gauge ring fails because one serial maps to one gauge. An honest agent pays 34 once and recovers the bond after audit.
